amendments.rule: **A subordinating conjunction the ASV supplies for a clause whose Hebrew writes none is `added`.** Casuistic law opens its protasis with אִם, with כִּי, or with a waw, and where one of these stands in the clause it takes the ASV's *if*, *when* or *that* by rules 14 and 30: the corpus aligns a waw to *if* and to *when*, and כִּי takes whichever of them the ASV has written for it. But the ASV also writes such a word for a clause that has no conjunction in it at all — *and, behold,* ***if*** *the plague be spread* for וְהִנֵּה פָּשָׂה הַנֶּגַע, and the italic ***yet*** of *he is bald,* ***yet*** *is he clean* for קֵרֵחַ הוּא טָהוֹר הוּא — and there no morpheme licenses it: it is its own `added` unit under rule 30. Do not fold it into the waw that opens the clause, into הִנֵּה, or into the verb, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also* — the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them, and the waw and הִנֵּה already have the *and* and the *behold* the ASV wrote for them. Count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's subordinators, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s, and mark whichever side is in surplus. **But a coordinator and a subordinator the ASV writes together for one waw are one rendering of that waw, and neither word is a surplus.** Where the ASV recasts a waw's own clause as a subordinate one and writes the pair at that clause's left edge — *And when I looked* for וָאֶרְאֶה, *And when I see the blood* for וְרָאִיתִי, and likewise *and that* and *so that* — both English words belong to the waw's single unit, and the count above marks nothing `added` unless no conjunction stands in the clause at all. Contiguity is the test, exactly as in rule 30: what makes the Leviticus *if* above a surplus is that הִנֵּה's *behold* stands between it and the waw's *and*, so the *if* is written beside those renderings rather than as part of one connective. Head such a unit on the coordinator, which is what the waw itself is; the corpus aligns a waw to *and when* in twenty-seven units, to *so that* in thirty-eight and to *and that* in eight, heading eleven of the *and when* units on *when* instead, so name that competing reading in the note under rule 8. An ASV italic on such a word corroborates it, and the absence of one is not evidence against it, by rule 7. **And a subordinator the ASV writes a second time for a clause coordinated under one the Hebrew has already written is that morpheme's own repeated realization, not a surplus.** Where a single אֲשֶׁר or כִּי governs coordinated clauses and the ASV rewrites its *that* at the head of a later one, every occurrence belongs to that morpheme's one possibly discontinuous unit under rule 25, exactly as a distributed `מִן` takes both of its *from*s there and a paraphrased suffix takes both of its pronouns under rule 18; head on the first, and mark nothing `added`. `לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יִגְבְּהוּ ... וְלֹא־יִתְּנוּ ... וְלֹא־יַעַמְדוּ` → *to the end* ***that*** *none ... exalt themselves ..., neither set their top ..., nor* ***that*** *their mighty ones stand up* gives both *that*s to the one אֲשֶׁר, the waws keeping only the *neither* and *nor* they are fused into. So read whether the later clause is coordinated under an earlier subordinator's scope before counting: what the count governs is a subordinator standing over a clause no written subordinator reaches, as the Leviticus protasis above has no conjunction in it at all. **And a word that belongs to a formula's own fixed English rendering is not a subordinator supplied for the clause: it belongs to the morpheme the formula rests on.** The oath חַי־אָנִי is written *As I live*, and the *As* is what English spends on the adverbial force of that predicate adjective, exactly as rule 20 takes the copula from the construction and rule 30 takes the pronouns of נָא's *I beseech thee* from the particle's one idiomatic rendering: the adjective takes *As … live* in one unit, discontinuous around the pronoun under rule 25 and headed on *live*, while an explicit אָנִי or אֲנִי takes only its own *I*. The corpus reads the formula this way in six chapters and never marks the *As* `added`. So before counting an English subordinator as a surplus, read whether it is one the formula always writes; the count above governs a word the ASV has supplied for the clause, not a word the formula's rendering contains.
amendments.why: EZK.31.14 met a case rule 55 and rule 25 both claim. A single אֲשֶׁר governs three coordinated purpose clauses and the ASV rewrites its complementizer at the head of the third (*to the end that none ... exalt themselves, neither set their top ..., nor that their mighty ones stand up*). Rule 25's distributed-function-word clause makes both *that*s one discontinuous unit on the אֲשֶׁר; rule 55's instruction to count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's subordinators, read on its own, would call the second one a surplus and mark it `added`. Leaving the collision unresolved would have every later pass decide it afresh, so the boundary is written into rule 55 itself rather than added as a cross-reference from a new rule. The qualification is narrow — it fires only where a subordinator the Hebrew actually writes has the later clause in its scope — and it rests on principle the contract already holds three times over: rule 25's `מִן` taking both of its *from*s, rule 18's suffix taking both of its pronouns, and rule 14's waw taking both members of a correlative pair. Nothing in the corpus tables supplied for this chapter bears against it. The rest of rule 55 is returned verbatim, including the coordinator-plus-subordinator passage with its corpus counts and its heading instruction, and the חַי־אָנִי formula passage.

conventions: דָּמָה carries the ASV's like, which is the verb's own lexeme, in all four of the chapter's comparison clauses (31.2, 31.8 twice, 31.18). The אֶל beside it takes only a separately written English word — unto in 31.8, To in 31.18 — and is unrepresented under rule 40 where the ASV writes none (31.2, and the second clause of 31.8). The fourth clause of 31.8, which writes like unto, is the internal evidence for the split; the BSB disagreement at 31.8 is this documented convention and not an error.

עֲבֹתִים → the thick boughs is headed on boughs throughout (31.3, 31.10, 31.14): thick is the ASV's specification of a word that already names the interlaced foliage, as sea monsters heads on monsters under rule 31. The competing head on thick is a genuine tie and is named in each unit's note under rule 8; head on boughs in any further Ezekiel occurrence rather than reopening it.

אֶרֶץ תַּחְתִּית → the nether parts of the earth is split the same way in 31.14, 31.16 and 31.18: the adjective תַּחְתִּי takes the nether parts with the phrase's supplied the, headed on the lexeme-bearing nether (rule 31), and אֶרֶץ takes of the earth (rule 19). No word of the recasting is added.

אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה → the Lord Jehovah (31.10, 31.15, 31.18): אֲדֹנָי takes the Lord with the supplied the under rule 15, and its 1cs suffix is unrepresented under rule 22, the ASV writing nothing separate for it. These are three of the chapter's four BSB disagreements and are a convention difference, not an error.

Both homographs of אֵת occur here, and MACULA's class is what tells them apart. The object marker H853 is tagged To (31.4 s015, 31.14, 31.15, 31.16) and is unrepresented under rule 16 wherever the ASV writes its object bare. The preposition אֵת with (H854) is tagged R (31.4 s007, 31.16 s014, 31.17, 31.18 twice); it aligns to the written with, and is unrepresented under rule 40 only at 31.4, where the ASV recasts the clause with the rivers as its subject. Read the class before citing a rule: 31.4's two occurrences are one of each.

report: Checked all 40 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for the `added` asymmetries the table cannot see. Nearly every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different clauses, which the source licenses: the הוּא suffixes follow the referent and the ASV's pronoun, בְּ and אֶל follow the written preposition, רַב is great or many as written, and the waw connectives (Thus 31.7, so that 31.9, even 31.11, yea 31.17, yet 31.18) are all rule 14 with corpus support.

The recurring constructions are consistent. Rule 29's the-counting holds in every construct chain: two written the's in 31.4, 31.5, 31.6, 31.12, 31.13 and 31.15 give the construct a supplied one and the article the one before its own word, while 31.9's single the goes to the present article on הָאֱלֹהִים and leaves גַן bare, and 31.8's articleless בְּגַן־אֱלֹהִים gives the same English string its supplied the on the construct. עֲבֹתִים heads on boughs in 31.3, 31.10 and 31.14 alike; אֶרֶץ תַּחְתִּית splits the same way in 31.14, 31.16 and 31.18; דָּמָה keeps like in all four of its clauses; the copula goes to a written הָיָה (31.7, 31.13) and to the preposition only where the clause is verbless (31.9).

One real finding, and it is the split the table flagged under אֵת. EZK.31.4 s007 is tagged R — the preposition אֵת with (H854) — but its note calls it the object marker and cites rule 16, which is the confusion rule 16's own closing sentence warns against; the same class is correctly read as the preposition in 31.16, 31.17 and 31.18. The status is unaffected, since the ASV recasts the clause with the rivers as its subject and spends no English word on the preposition, leaving it unrepresented under rule 40 either way. The patch to EZK.31.4 therefore keeps every edge and every head unchanged and corrects only the s007 and s015 notes and the verse's review notes.

BSB: none of the four disagreements is an error. 31.8 אֶל is the דָּמָה convention, and the chapter carries its own proof — the fourth clause of 31.8 writes like unto, so the verb has like and the preposition has unto, which is why the second clause's preposition has nothing. The three אֲדֹנָי suffixes (31.10, 31.15, 31.18) are rule 22: the ASV writes the Lord and nothing separate for the suffix. No accepted edge was changed to move the rate.

Two places worth naming for a later reader. 31.15 בְּיוֹם רִדְתּוֹ is rule 52's closing clause — the בְּ stands on יוֹם and already has In, so the when falls to the infinitive as nomen rectum, and 31.5 and 31.16, where the preposition does stand on the infinitive, take the when themselves. And 31.14's two neither/nor are two separate waw-plus-negative fusions rather than one correlative pair on a single waw, which is what rule 14's counting requires.

The amendment below settles 31.14's twice-written that. The single אֲשֶׁר governs three coordinated purpose clauses and the ASV rewrites its complementizer at the head of the third; rule 25 makes both occurrences that morpheme's one discontinuous unit, but rule 55's instruction to count subordinators against conjunctions would mark the second one added. Rule 55 is the rule that needed the boundary, so it is amended rather than qualified from outside.
